//: What each function of Kurve must reach against the reference (tools/ref/README.md): tol, a relative error (floor, an absolute one beside it for values near zero); until, the slice of ux/spec/PARITY_SPEC.md that brings a function short of its target there; now, the worst error it was measured at when that was written, which it must not pass; why, what keeps it short. Read by tools/ref-test.mjs and tools/ref/diff-fuzz.py.

norris.lmFit.why: a straight line fitted by Levenberg–Marquardt with a numerical Jacobian; 4.1 solves linear models by QR

quantileType.why: the interpolation weight carries the rounding of p(n + 1 - a - b), which the gap between the two values it lies between multiplies; R's is the same

descStats.shape.why: skewness and kurtosis are differences of terms of order 1: judged by their absolute error below 1

swTest.p.why: p is Φ of a function of ln(1 − W), which multiplies an error in W by 1/(1 − W)

ksnTest.p.why: Kolmogorov's tail; Miller's 2·one-sided where n·d² passes 2.2 (kolmogN.sf)

adTest.a2.why: A² is a sum of n logarithms cancelling to a small number: its relative error grows with n over A²

kolmogN.sf.why: past n·x² = 2.2 the tail is Miller's twice the one-sided tail (SciPy's too), which leaves out both sides at once; below, 1 − P(D ≤ x)

kolmogN.pg.why: the reference is SciPy's Pelz and Good expansion (1e-9 off at 5000 values) where Durbin's matrix in 40 digits is too slow to make; Kurve's is the matrix

tTest1.ci.why: an interval's end is the estimate plus or minus q·se: near zero they cancel

tTest1.dci.why: the noncentral t inverted, against Boost's inverted by brentq

tTest2.ci.why: an interval's end is the estimate plus or minus q·se: near zero they cancel

tTest2.dci.why: the noncentral t inverted, against Boost's inverted by brentq

tTestPaired.ci.why: an interval's end is the estimate plus or minus q·se: near zero they cancel

tTestPaired.dci.why: the noncentral t inverted, against Boost's inverted by brentq

fisher22.ci.why: a bound of a small odds ratio, solved by halving in log ψ

nctCdf.why: absolute: the series subtracts far in the lower tail of a negative t, where only absolute accuracy holds (what an interval needs)

anovaComp.q.p.why: against SciPy's studentized range, off by up to 5e-14 absolutely (two such cases in 40 digits: Kurve right to 3e-15); range.json holds the 40-digit tails

anovaComp.q.ci.why: SciPy's quantile is a root found to its own tolerance

nist.anova.why: against the exact answer for the doubles NIST's decimals parse to; the certified values are printed beside as digits right

ks2Test.p.why: SciPy's exact two-sample distribution, itself checked only to about 1e-13 here

corrTest.r.why: Exact rationals with one square root in 40 digits (refs.py)

spearmanTest.rho.why: Exact rationals with one square root in 40 digits (refs.py)

kendallTau.tau.why: Exact rationals with one square root in 40 digits (refs.py)

partialCorr.r.why: The inverse of the exact correlation matrix in 40 digits; an r near 0 judged absolutely

corrTest.p.why: The t tail (or Kendall's exact count, or the normal) of the exact statistic, in 40 digits

spearmanTest.p.why: The t tail (or Kendall's exact count, or the normal) of the exact statistic, in 40 digits

kendallTau.p.why: The t tail (or Kendall's exact count, or the normal) of the exact statistic, in 40 digits

partialCorr.p.why: The t tail (or Kendall's exact count, or the normal) of the exact statistic, in 40 digits

corrTest.ci.why: Fisher's z interval of the exact r, in 40 digits

chi2Indep.X2.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

chi2Indep.G.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

chi2Indep.V.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

chi2Indep.p.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

chi2Indep.pG.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

fisherRC.p.why: Freeman–Halton's sum in rationals; Kurve's in logarithms relative to the observed table

mcnemarTest.X2.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

mcnemarTest.p.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

mcnemarTest.pExact.why: Exact rationals (refs.py), the tails in 40 digits

linModel.b.why: Exact rationals (refs.py lm_ref): the coefficients by Householder QR refined on the augmented system in double-double

linModel.se.why: The covariance refined in double-double (on XᵀX, then the augmented system where that does not settle)

linModel.t.why: Exact rationals (refs.py lm_ref): the coefficients by Householder QR refined on the augmented system in double-double

linModel.p.why: The t and F tails of the exact statistics, in 40 digits

linModel.ci.why: The estimate less t times its error: judged against the estimate's size plus the half-width

linModel.s.why: The residuals in double-double, the solution kept in double-double

linModel.rss.why: The residuals in double-double, the solution kept in double-double

linModel.r2.why: Sums of squares as the squared difference of two fits' residuals: nothing cancels

linModel.F.why: Sums of squares as the squared difference of two fits' residuals, or by Wald's identity on the refined covariance

linModel.ss.why: Type I from prefixes of one QR, refined; II and III by Wald's identity, or refits where columns are aliased

lmContrast.est.why: Σ L·b of the refined solution, judged against its size plus its error (a contrast near 0 is a difference)

lmContrast.se.why: Lᵀ V L of the refined covariance

lmEst.est.why: An estimated mean or a difference of them: L·b of the refined solution against exact rationals (a difference judged against its size plus its error)

lmEst.se.why: √(LᵀVL·s²) of the refined covariance against exact rationals

lmWaldL.F.why: Wald's F of the simple effects against exact rationals

rmAnova.ss.why: Integer Helmert contrasts summed in double-double, the regression refined: against rational projections

rmAnova.F.why: Ratios of those sums of squares

rmAnova.eps.why: Greenhouse–Geisser's and Huynh–Feldt's ε from the residuals' covariance, against its rational traces

rmAnova.W.why: Mauchly's W: det(BᵀEB)/det(BᵀB) on a rational basis

rmAnova.x2.why: −f ln W: near W = 1 the logarithm magnifies W's last digit

rmAnova.p.why: F's tail (df scaled by ε) and χ²'s, in 40 digits

DIST.ncf.sf.why: A Poisson mixture of incomplete betas, every term positive: both tails keep their relative digits; each term carries the central tail's error (1e-13), 2.4e-14 seen at 5e-36

DIST.ncf.cdf.why: The same mixture of the lower tails; each term carries the central tail's error (1e-13), 2.4e-14 seen at 5e-36

DIST.ncx2.sf.why: A Poisson mixture of incomplete gammas, every term positive; each term carries the central tail's error (1e-13), 2.4e-14 seen at 5e-36

DIST.ncx2.cdf.why: The same mixture of the lower tails; each term carries the central tail's error (1e-13), 2.4e-14 seen at 5e-36

DIST.nct.sf.why: Guenther's sum (nctCdf), 1 less it: relative where the tail is not small

powerAt.why: Absolute: the tails at quantiles worked out to 1e-15, against 60 digits

powSize.n.why: The smallest size reaching the power, exactly

rocTest.se.why: DeLong's variance from deviations that are exact multiples of a half over n₁n₀

rocTest.youden.why: Youden's J compared as integers; the cut-off a score itself

rocCompare.why: The difference of two areas, DeLong's SE from the exact differences of their deviations, z and the normal tail
